title: 9. The Queen of the Field Mice

paragraphs.en: The Scarecrow noted they were close to the yellow brick road as they had traveled nearly as far as the river had carried them.
paragraphs.zh: 稻草人注意到他们离那条黄色砖路已经很近了，因为他们几乎走了和河水带他们同样远的距离。

paragraphs.en: Suddenly, a low growl caught the Tin Woodman's attention. He turned to see a large yellow Wildcat bounding towards them. The cat's ears lay flat against its head, and it showed ugly teeth with red eyes glowing like fire.
paragraphs.zh: 突然，一阵低沉的咆哮声吸引了铁皮木人注意。他转头看见一只大黄野猫朝他们奔来。那猫的耳朵紧贴在脑袋上，露出丑陋的牙齿，红眼睛像火一样闪烁着。

paragraphs.en: Behind the beast ran a small gray field mouse.
paragraphs.zh: 在那头野兽身后，有一只小小的灰色田鼠ksz。

paragraphs.en: The Woodman raised his axe and struck the Wildcat, severing its head from its body. The creature fell into two pieces at his feet.
paragraphs.zh: 樵夫高举斧头，朝野猫砍去，将其首级与身体分离。野猫的身躯在他脚下一分为二。

paragraphs.en: The freed field mouse thanked the Tin Woodman in a squeaky voice. Despite having no heart, the Woodman insisted it was his duty to help those in need, even if they were just mice.
paragraphs.zh: 被释放的田鼠用尖细的声音向锡木人道谢。尽管没有心脏，锡木人坚持认为帮助有需要的人是他的职责，哪怕对方只是些老鼠。

paragraphs.en: "Only a mouse!" the little animal indignantly corrected. "I am the Queen of all Field Mice!"
paragraphs.zh: “我只是只老鼠！”小动物愤愤地纠正道，“我是田鼠女王！”

paragraphs.en: The Woodman bowed and acknowledged her claim. The Queen declared that by saving her life, he had performed both a brave and great deed.
paragraphs.zh: 樵夫躬身表示认可。女王宣布，他救了自己的命，既勇敢又伟大。

paragraphs.en: Several field mice soon arrived, bowing so low to their Queen they almost stood on their heads. They asked how she escaped the Wildcat. The Queen explained that the Tin Woodman had killed the beast and saved her life, and from now on, all the mice must serve him and obey his wishes.
paragraphs.zh: 几只田鼠很快便到了，它们向女王低下了头，几乎要倒立起来。田鼠们询问她是如何躲过野猫的。女王解释说，是铁皮木人杀死了那只野兽并救了她的命，从今以后，所有的田鼠都必须效忠于他，并遵从他的意愿。

paragraphs.en: The mice agreed with enthusiasm, scurrying off in all directions. Toto, awakened from his nap, barked joyfully and joined them. The Tin Woodman held him back, calling out, "Come back!
paragraphs.zh: 田鼠们热情地同意了，四散奔去。托托从午睡中醒来，兴奋地叫了起来，加入了它们的行列。锡人木匠用力拉住了他，喊道：“回来！”

paragraphs.en: Come back! Toto won't hurt you."
paragraphs.zh: 回来吧！托托不会伤害你。

paragraphs.en: From beneath the grass, the Queen of the Mice peeked out timidly. "Are you sure he won’t bite us?" she asked.
paragraphs.zh: 从草丛下探出头来，田鼠女王怯生生地问道：“你确定他不会咬我们吗？”

paragraphs.en: "I will not let him," said the Woodman reassuringly. The mice returned one by one as Toto remained quiet, trying to break free but knowing his tin body prevented it.
paragraphs.zh: “我不会让他这么做。”伐木工宽慰地说。田鼠们一个接一个地返回，托托则安静地尝试挣脱，明知自己的锡制身体无法如愿。

paragraphs.en: Finally, a large mouse spoke up. "Can we do anything to repay you for saving our Queen?"
paragraphs.zh: 终于，一只较大的田鼠开口说道：“我们能为您救回我们的女王做点什么以表感谢吗？”

paragraphs.en: The Woodman replied, "Not that I know of." But the Scarecrow, still struggling with his thoughts due to his straw-filled head, quickly added, "Yes; help us save the Cowardly Lion in the poppy field."
paragraphs.zh: 木匠回答说：“据我所知没有。”但稻草人仍然因为脑袋里装满了稻草而思绪纷乱，连忙补充道：“是的；帮我们救救罂粟花田里的胆小狮吧。”

paragraphs.en: "Is there a lion?" cried the little Queen. "He would eat us all!"
paragraphs.zh: “有没有狮子？”小女王喊道，“他会把我们全都吃掉！”

paragraphs.en: "No," declared the Scarecrow. "This Lion is a coward." The Mouse asked, "Really?"
paragraphs.zh: “不,”稻草人断言道,“这只狮子是胆小鬼。”田鼠问道:“真的吗?”

paragraphs.en: "He says so himself," said the Scarecrow. "He won't hurt anyone who's our friend. If you help save him, I promise he'll be kind to you."
paragraphs.zh: “他自己也这么说的，”稻草人说道，“他不会伤害任何我们的朋友。如果你帮助救了他，我保证他会对你友善。”

paragraphs.en: The Queen agreed, trusting them. She asked, "How many mice obey me?" and was told there were thousands.
paragraphs.zh: 女王同意了，信任他们的话。她问道：“有多少老鼠听我的命令？”得到的回答是成千上万只。

paragraphs.en: "Send for all of them with a long piece of string," instructed the Scarecrow. The attending mice immediately dispersed to gather their people.
paragraphs.zh: “把它们全都叫来，用一根长绳子拴着，”稻草人吩咐道。那些小田鼠立刻四散开来，去召集自己的同类。

paragraphs.en: Turning to the Woodman, the Scarecrow said, "You must make a truck by the riverside to carry the Lion."
paragraphs.zh: 对木匠说，稻草人说道：“你必须在河边造一辆卡车，用来运输狮子。”

paragraphs.en: The Woodman quickly prepared a cart by chopping tree limbs and fastening them with wooden pegs, creating four wheels from a large trunk. By the time the field mice arrived, the cart was ready.
paragraphs.zh: 伐木工迅速砍下树枝，用木钉固定，从一棵大树上削出四个轮子，制成了一辆手推车。等田鼠们赶到时，手推车已经准备好了。

paragraphs.en: Thousands of mice—big, small, and medium-sized—gathered, each carrying a piece of string. Dorothy woke up to find herself surrounded by these tiny creatures. The Scarecrow introduced her as "Her Majesty" to the Queen mouse, who curtsied and soon became friendly with Dorothy.
paragraphs.zh: 成千上万的老鼠——有大有小，还有中等大小的——聚集在一起，每只老鼠都拿着一段线。多萝西醒来时发现自己被这些小生物团团围住。稻草人将她介绍给田鼠女王为“陛下来宾”，女王行了一个礼，并很快与多萝西熟络了起来。

paragraphs.en: The Scarecrow and Woodman tied strings around the mice's necks, attaching them to the cart. Despite its size, the mice pulled it easily. Even the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman could ride on it as they drew the Lion from his slumber in the poppy field.
paragraphs.zh: 稻草人和铁皮木人给田鼠系上了绳子，将它们固定在手推车上。尽管田鼠体型不大，却轻松地拉动着车。就连稻草人和铁皮木人也能坐在上面，随着他们把狮子从罂粟花田中唤醒而一起前行。

paragraphs.en: With much effort, they managed to load the heavy Lion onto the cart. The Queen ordered her subjects to start moving before they fell asleep like the flowers around them. Many mice struggled with the heavily loaded cart, but with help from the Woodman and Scarecrow, they eventually rolled the Lion out of the poppy field into greener pastures.
paragraphs.zh: 经过一番努力，他们终于把那只沉重的狮子装上了马车。女王命令她的臣民们赶紧出发，否则他们会像周围的花朵一样睡着了。尽管载重的马车给许多田鼠带来了不小的负担，但在樵木人和稻草人的帮助下，大家最终还是将狮子从罂粟地里推到了一片更加肥沃的土地上。

paragraphs.en: Dorothy thanked the mice for saving the Lion, who had become a dear friend to her.
paragraphs.zh: 多萝西感谢田鼠们救了狮子，而今这位狮子成了她亲密的朋友。

paragraphs.en: The mice scampered away through the grass to their homes. The Queen of the Mice was the last to leave. "If ever you need us again," she said, "come out into the field and call, and we shall hear you and come to your assistance."
paragraphs.zh: 田鼠们匆匆穿过草地回到各自的家。作为田鼠之王的她最后才离开。“如果你们再次需要我们，”她说，“就来到田间呼救，我们会听到并前来援助。”

paragraphs.en: She then ran off.
paragraphs.zh: 她随后飞快地跑了出去。

paragraphs.en: Dorothy held Toto tightly as the Queen departed, fearing he might run after her. The group sat beside the Lion until he awakened. Meanwhile, the Scarecrow brought Dorothy some fruit from a nearby tree for her lunch.
paragraphs.zh: 多萝西紧紧抱着托托，目送女王离开，担心托托会追上去。大家坐在狮子身边，等待它苏醒。这时，稻草人从附近的一棵树上摘了一些水果给多萝西做午餐。
